one_month_reasoning: No Nutanix earnings fall in the window: Q1 FY27 results are expected Nov 24 to Dec 2, 2026, after Oct 31 (supervisor check of aggregator calendars). The President/CCO leaves on Oct 2, but this was disclosed in an 8-K on Sep 24, so it is known news. The Oct 27-28 FOMC is the main macro event. Odds of an October hike are now below 50%: CME FedWatch showed roughly 35-47% on Sep 30, depending on the snapshot, after dovish remarks from the NY Fed president. Kalshi still showed a higher figure, so the market odds conflict. That corrects the stale 56% I used in round 1, and either outcome is close to priced. Momentum after the Q4 beat and reversal after the run from about $38 to $70 roughly offset each other. I therefore keep a symmetric lognormal centred at about $70.8 (flat) with a monthly sigma of 13% (47% annual vol / 3.5).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of P/E (FY28 non-GAAP diluted EPS of about $2.70 x 26x = $70.2) and EV/FCF (FY28 FCF of about $1.03B x 18x = $18.5B EV). For the EV/FCF method I add gross cash of $2.36B over 292.7M if-converted diluted shares ($71.4), cross-checked by treating the 2029 notes as debt ($1.50B net cash over 282.6M shares, $70.9), and take $71.2. The blend is $70.7, which I round to $70.5.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (NTM at Oct-2027) non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.70 x 26x

inputs_detail.derivation: Revenue of about $3.60B (FY27 guide midpoint $3.205B +12%; consensus FY28 is $3.65B) x a non-GAAP operating margin of about 25.5% (FY27 guide 24-25%, moving toward the FY29 targets), plus about $70M of other income, taxed at the company's fixed 20% rate, over about 292M diluted shares, gives about $2.70. My round-1 figure of $2.66 (consensus +15%) was close. The supervisor's tax-rate rebuild confirms this level.

Raised from 25x. Today's price is 30.6x FY27 consensus and about 26.2x FY28E. Round 1's 25x leaned on October hike odds of about 56%. CME FedWatch now puts those below 50% (about 35-47% on Sep 30), though rates are still restrictive (3.75-4.00% after the Sep 16 hike) and a later hike remains possible. I keep a modest discount to today's multiple for that, for SBC (12.5% of revenue) and for NTNX's history of re-rating down on guidance cuts.

methods.inputs: FY28 FCF $1.03B x 18x EV/FCF = EV $18.54B. Plus gross cash of $2.36B over 292.7M if-converted diluted shares = $71.4. Alternative: plus $1.50B net cash (2029 notes treated as debt) over 282.6M shares = $70.9. Average $71.2.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 revenue of about $3.6B at about 28.5% FCF margin, the high-20s FY29 target. Cross-check: MarketScreener consensus FY28 FCF is $1.036B.

inputs_detail.derivation: Corrected from round 1, where I deducted the $1.35B principal and also used the diluted count, counting the converts twice (about -$4.6/share). Now: gross cash over 292.7M shares, or, treating the out-of-the-money 2029 notes as debt, $1.50B net cash over 282.6M shares.

NTNX's EV/FCF ran 20.4x in FY24, 26.4x in FY25 and 18.4x in FY26. I take the lower-middle of that range because SBC is excluded from FCF and rates are still restrictive. I left this unchanged: the correction is to the cash bridge, not to the multiple.

bear.story: This repeats the late-2025 pattern. The stock slid from $72.4 (Nov 10, 2025) to $58.8 ahead of the Q1 report, fell 18% to $48.3 on the guidance cut, and troughed at $46.6 (Dec 2). The cumulative drawdown was about 35% over about three weeks, though only the 18% was the event-day move. Here, supply constraints worse than the guide already assumes, sales disruption after the CCO's exit, or stalled VMware migrations (VDDK friction, Proxmox/OpenShift) cut growth to below 10%. The multiple compresses to about 18-19x on about $2.35 EPS.

base.story: Nutanix delivers its FY27 guide of about 12% growth, a 24-25% margin and $850-950M FCF, which already assumes server/DRAM constraints all year. ARR grows in the mid-teens and NRR holds at about 106%. The price compounds with EPS to about 27x FY28 EPS of $2.70, and the cash pile supports buybacks that offset SBC.

bull.story: VMware displacement accelerates through the 2026-27 renewal cycles, the external-storage and AMD/NVIDIA AI deals add growth, and guidance is raised toward the mid-to-high-teens FY29 targets. Supply eases in 2027, and the stock re-rates to about 33x FY28 EPS of about $2.95-3.05.

thesis_break_reason: $46 is about 17x FY28E EPS of $2.70 and about 11x FY28 FCF ex gross cash ($46 x 292.7M = $13.5B market cap, less $2.36B cash = $11.1B EV, against $1.03B FCF). It is also below the post-guide-cut trough of $46.6-47.8 (Dec 2025) and the June 2026 low of about $46.5. The FY27 guide already assumes supply constraints for the whole year. A sustained move to $46 without a market-wide sell-off would therefore most likely mean that guide has failed (demand or sales execution after the CCO's exit), not ordinary 47%-vol noise.

reasoning: Base rates are unchanged from round 1. NTNX's 70 rolling 12-month returns (monthly closes, 2019-2026) have a median of +21% with an IQR of -12% to +62%, and 64% are positive. Realized vol is about 47-50%. I do not carry that drift forward, because it reflects the 2023-24 re-rating from a cash-burning to an FCF-positive company. The supervisor's findings change three things. (1) The cash bridge: the 292.7M diluted count already includes both convertibles under the if-converted method, so my round-1 EV/FCF method double-counted $1.35B of notes. Corrected, it is $71.2, not $66.8. (2) Macro: the 56% October hike odds I used came from a secondary blog dated Sep 20. CME FedWatch was about 35-47% on Sep 30, so I lift my P/E multiple from 25x to 26x but keep it below today's ~30.6x FY27 multiple, because policy is still restrictive. FY28 EPS of $2.70, rebuilt at the company's 20% non-GAAP tax rate, is close to my $2.66. (3) The guidance-cut precedent: I checked Twelve Data daily closes. The stock fell 18% on the report day ($58.8 to $48.3) after already drifting down from $72.4. The full peak-to-trough fall was still about 35%, so the left tail stays, but the event-day hit is smaller than I implied. The guide now embeds supply constraints, which lowers the chance of a repeat. I trim the left-tail mixture's weight slightly and centre it a little higher. Fair value is now $70.5, essentially at spot. The ladder is a mixture: 80% lognormal with a median of $73.5 (sigma 0.40) and 20% left-tail with a median of $59 (sigma 0.5). That gives a median of about $71 (previously $69.5) and P(>=71) of 0.50. The scenario mean of about $73 is consistent with it. I did not copy the supervisor ladder: mine is slightly lower in the middle because I keep a below-spot multiple and an explicit guidance-cut tail. Research this round was limited to 2 checks (Twelve Data prices and a FedWatch search).
